decision: Keep derived meshes and scans local until the authors clarify the conflicting research-only ethics language for the intended public potentially commercial atlas.

sources.title: Bolelli et al. (2026), Multi-structure segmentation in CBCT volumes: The ToothFairy2 challenge

sources.finding: The current author publication explicitly says the training data are available under CC BY-SA and that this license permits third-party redistribution. The institutional repository is described as the authoritative maintained source; contributing derived data there is encouraged rather than mandated.

sources.finding: The ethics section restricts sharing to research purposes. The same page also declares the data CC BY-SA. The later publication names the same ethics approval 1374/2020/OSS/ESTMO SIRER ID 1275 but does not explicitly address removal or scope of this research-only sentence.

sources.title: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International
sources.finding: The copyright license permits commercial sharing and adaptation with attribution and ShareAlike. It does not necessarily supply all other permissions, including privacy or publicity rights.

assessment: There is strong current primary evidence for commercial-compatible copyright licensing and redistribution. The old ethics text is a separate unresolved inconsistency, not evidence that the license is CC BY-NC. Treating that text as automatically cancelled would be an inference not expressly supported by the reviewed author materials.
scope: Conservative publication decision for the user's explicit requirement of later unrestricted commercial-compatible publication; no legal guarantee is made. Local research and geometry inspection remain useful.
